name: BottomNav
description: A tab bar for the bottom of a phone-sized screen: three to five main places, each with an icon and a short label, the current one marked. It keeps clear of the home indicator, has touch-sized targets, and can show a count on a tab. It comes plain or as a floating bar.

items.description: The tabs as data: { id, label, href?, icon?, badge?, permission? }. Three to five fit well. Sub-items (children) are ignored: a tab bar is one level. An item may carry a permission ("allow", "disabled", "hidden" or { state, reason }): hidden items are not drawn; disabled items stay as focusable, non-navigating entries (aria-disabled) with the reason read out.

currentId.description: The id of the place you are on. It is marked as the current page (aria-current) and drawn with a pill behind its icon and a heavier label.

onNavigate.description: Called with the item when one is chosen. Items without an href use this to do their work.

renderLink.description: Draw the tabs as your router's link. Return the link with the given className and children; call onClick when chosen. Without it, items with an href are plain links.
renderLink.tsType: (props: { item: import("../sidebar/nav").NavItem; className: string; children: import("react").ReactNode; isCurrent: boolean; onClick: () => void }) => import("react").ReactNode

labels.description: always: every tab shows its label. active: only the current tab does. never: icons only. A hidden label is still the tab's name for screen readers, so every item needs a label.

variant.description: plain: a bar across the full width with a line above it. floating: a rounded bar with a shadow and a margin around it.

fixed.description: Pin the bar to the bottom of the screen. Leave room for it at the bottom of the page yourself. Without it the bar sits in the flow, for example at the bottom of a framed app.

classNames.description: Class names for the parts, by slot name, added after the built-in ones. Slots: root, list, item, icon, label, badge.

keyboard: Tab: moves through the tabs in order
Enter or Space: follows a link or runs the tab's action
requirements: The tabs are inside one named navigation landmark and form a list of links, not a tablist: they go to other places, they do not switch panels of this page
The current place is marked with aria-current="page" and also drawn with a pill behind the icon and a heavier label, never by color alone
Every tab has a name even when its label is hidden (labels active or never)
A count on a tab is read after the label ("Inbox, 3") and the visual count is hidden from screen readers
A disabled tab stays focusable (aria-disabled), goes nowhere and says why
Each tab is at least 44 by 44 CSS pixels
The bar keeps clear of the home indicator with the bottom safe-area inset
Hover, focus and the current mark respect reduced motion
screenReader: "Main navigation, navigation", then each tab as a link; the current one reads "Home, current page"
"Inbox, 3, link" for a tab with a count
A hidden label is still read: "Search, link"

use_when: The main places of an app on a phone: home, search, inbox, account
Places people move between often and want one tap away
avoid_when: More than five places: group the rest behind a More tab, or use Sidebar in a sheet
Switching between views of one page: use Tabs
A wide screen: use TopNav or Sidebar and show BottomNav only on narrow screens
anti_patterns: A different set of tabs on different pages: the bar is the same everywhere in the app
Icon-only tabs that nobody can tell apart: keep the labels unless the icons are universal
Using it as a toolbar for page actions: tabs go to places, buttons do things
UI permission is not security: hiding or disabling a tab only changes what people see, so the server must check access again for every request
